description: Postgraduate systems analysis: systems and soft-systems thinking, feasibility and business cases, process, data and object-oriented modelling, the step to design, and a critical comparison of development methodologies. Students model real organisational problems in the diagram studio, defend their analysis in stakeholder scenarios, and write a consultancy report.
modelledOn: Dennis, Wixom and Roth, Systems Analysis and Design
Checkland and Scholes, Soft Systems Methodology in Action
Object Management Group, UML 2.5 and BPMN 2.0 specifications
Valacich and George, Modern Systems Analysis and Design
outcomes: Frame an ill-structured organisational problem with systems and soft-systems methods and identify stakeholders and their concerns.
Assess feasibility and build a financial and risk-based business case for an information system.
Produce consistent process, data and object-oriented models and verify them against each other.
Translate analysis models into architecture and design decisions, weighing quality-attribute trade-offs.
Compare development methodologies and justify a choice for a given project context.
Write and defend a systems analysis report for a real organisation, including model validation and a change plan.

units.title: Systems thinking and soft systems methods
topics: General systems theory: boundaries, environment, feedback loops and emergence
Soft systems methodology: rich pictures, CATWOE and root definitions
Hard versus soft problems; wicked problems and the limits of optimisation
Stakeholder analysis: power-interest grids, concerns and conflicts
Sociotechnical systems: people, process and technology, with examples from cooperatives and market associations in Ghana

units.title: Investigation, feasibility and project selection
topics: Requirements elicitation: interviews, observation, workshops and questionnaires
Feasibility dimensions: technical, economic, operational, schedule and legal
Economic analysis: net present value, payback period, return on investment and sensitivity analysis
Project selection and portfolio scoring against strategic criteria
Risk identification and the business case document

units.title: Process and logic modelling
topics: Levelled data flow diagrams: context diagram, decomposition and balancing
BPMN 2.0: pools, lanes, events, gateways and message flow
Process analysis: bottlenecks, cycle time and queueing with Little law
Decision tables, decision trees and structured English for business rules
Process redesign: business process re-engineering, lean waste removal and automation candidates
Exceptions and compensation in workflows; process simulation

units.title: Data modelling
topics: Entity-relationship and extended ER models: generalisation, weak entities and cardinality
Normalisation to third normal form and Boyce-Codd normal form
From conceptual to logical to physical data models
Data dictionary and the CRUD matrix linking processes to data
Data quality, master data, migration and legacy-system integration
Dimensional models for management reporting

units.title: Object-oriented analysis with UML
topics: Use case modelling: actors, scenarios, extend and include relationships
Class diagrams: associations, aggregation, composition, generalisation and OCL constraints
Interaction diagrams: sequence and communication diagrams
Activity and state machine diagrams for behaviour
Domain models, CRC cards and responsibility assignment patterns
Consistency checking across models: traceability from use case to class to table

units.title: From analysis to design
topics: Architecture styles: layered, service-oriented, microservices and event-driven
Mapping analysis models to design: classes to tables, use cases to services
User interface prototyping and usability evaluation
Non-functional requirements and quality-attribute trade-offs
Build, buy or outsource: package selection, ERP and open-source options

units.title: Development methodologies compared
topics: Plan-driven methods: waterfall and the V-model
Iterative methods: prototyping, spiral and the unified process
Agile methods: Scrum, Kanban and extreme programming
DevOps and continuous delivery as an operating model
Selecting and tailoring a methodology: project size, risk, regulation and team skills
Methodologies in context: public sector tendering versus a mobile money start-up

units.title: Enterprise perspective, validation and change
topics: Enterprise architecture frameworks: Zachman and TOGAF layers
System dynamics: stock-and-flow diagrams, feedback loops and simulation of policy effects
Verification and validation of models: walkthroughs, inspection and animation
Implementation: change management, training, conversion strategies and post-implementation review
Capstone: analysis report and defence for a real organisation

schedule.title: Soft systems and stakeholders
schedule.exercise: Draw a rich picture of a market traders cooperative that wants a digital ledger, write root definitions with CATWOE and place six stakeholders on a power-interest grid.

tasks.title: Draw a rich picture of a district hospital outpatient department showing actors, concerns, conflicts and information flows
Work a cooperative case in the scenario engine, choosing CATWOE elements from interview evidence and scoring root definitions against the rubric
Resolve conflicting stakeholder demands in a school fees system case, ranking concerns and justifying which are met, deferred or refused

schedule.title: Feasibility, elicitation and the business case
schedule.exercise: Prepare an interview guide, compute NPV and payback for a mobile money agent system over five years, and write a one-page business case.

tasks.title: Compute NPV, payback period and return on investment for a clinic records system from a cash flow table and recommend go or no go
Interview a simulated stakeholder panel, select questions to uncover hidden requirements and score the completeness of the requirement list you capture
Assess three competing projects with scoring, risk and sensitivity analysis, and defend the portfolio choice when the budget covers only two

schedule.title: Data flow, BPMN and process analysis
schedule.exercise: Draw a context diagram and level 1 DFD for a licence renewal service, model it in BPMN, and find its bottleneck from timing data.

tasks.title: Draw a context diagram and level 1 data flow diagram for a vehicle licence renewal office and run the balancing check
Model a loan approval with a pool for each party, two gateways and a timer event in BPMN, and validate against the structural rules
Apply Little law and an M/M/1 queue to measured arrival and service times, find the bottleneck step and predict waiting time after adding a clerk

schedule.title: Business rules and process redesign
schedule.exercise: Convert a policy paragraph into a decision table, remove contradictions, and propose a redesigned process with waste and automation marked.

tasks.title: Write a decision table for a mobile money transaction limit policy and verify each rule combination is complete and exclusive
Redraw a paper-based permit process as a leaner BPMN model, marking removed hand-offs and counting expected days saved
Simulate a workflow with rework loops by Monte Carlo and compare mean completion time with and without a redesigned exception path

schedule.title: Entity-relationship modelling and normalisation
schedule.exercise: Model a farm cooperative with an ER diagram including a generalisation, normalise a messy order table to BCNF and write the physical schema.

tasks.title: Draw an ER diagram for a farmers cooperative with members, plots, deliveries and payments, labelling keys and cardinalities
Normalise a single order table with repeating groups to third normal form and check the decomposition is lossless by joining it back
Turn a conceptual model with a subtype hierarchy into three alternative relational designs and compare their queries and storage on sample data

schedule.title: Data dictionary, quality and reporting models
schedule.exercise: Produce a CRUD matrix tying processes to entities, find the data quality problems in a legacy extract and sketch a star schema for monthly reports.

tasks.title: Build a CRUD matrix between six processes and five entities and flag entities that are never created or never read
Profile a legacy customer table with SQL to find duplicates, nulls and invalid phone formats, and write the clean-up queries
Design a star schema for district sales reporting and load sample data, then write three management queries against it and check totals

schedule.title: Use cases, class diagrams and interactions
schedule.exercise: Write use case descriptions for a school fees portal, derive a class diagram with an OCL constraint, and draw a sequence diagram for payment.

tasks.title: Draw a use case diagram for an online school fees portal with three actors, and write one full scenario description
Derive a class diagram from the portal use cases, with multiplicities and one OCL constraint, and check each noun has a purpose
Draw sequence diagrams for the payment use case with a failure path and verify every message maps to a class operation

schedule.title: Behaviour models and model consistency
schedule.exercise: Model the life cycle of a fee payment as a state machine, assign responsibilities with CRC cards, and trace one requirement through all models.

tasks.title: Draw a state machine for a fee payment moving from pending through confirmed, failed and refunded, with guards on transitions
Create CRC cards for six classes in a library system and walk three scenarios to find missing responsibilities
Check a given set of DFD, ER, class and sequence models for five planted inconsistencies and list which model needs to change in each case

schedule.title: From analysis to design
schedule.exercise: Choose an architecture for a national health claims system, map analysis models to design, and justify a build-or-buy decision using weighted criteria.

tasks.title: Draw a layered architecture for a school portal, placing each analysis class in a layer and marking its interfaces
Resolve a conflict between performance, cost and security requirements in a claims system case and score the trade-off argument
Evaluate three ERP options for a mid-sized cooperative on cost, fit, local support and lock-in, and defend the recommendation to a panel

schedule.title: Plan-driven and iterative methods
schedule.exercise: Compare waterfall, spiral and Scrum on one project with changing requirements, and compute how late defect discovery raises cost under each.

tasks.title: Draw the V-model and map each development phase to its test level for a payroll system
Plan three spiral iterations for a risky mobile money integration on a Gantt chart, showing the risk addressed in each
Run a case where a sponsor demands fixed scope and dates; choose and defend a delivery method and contract form, scored by rubric

schedule.title: Choosing and tailoring a methodology
schedule.exercise: Write a methodology recommendation memo for two contrasting projects, a tax authority system and a mobile money start-up app, naming the practices adopted.

tasks.title: Draw a delivery pipeline from commit to production for a small team, labelling automated tests and approval gates
Select a methodology for four projects of different size, risk and regulation using a decision matrix and check against expert answers
Tailor a methodology for a public tender with legal milestones and agile delivery, resolving conflicts between contract rules and iteration

schedule.title: Enterprise architecture and system dynamics
schedule.exercise: Place an existing system in the TOGAF layers, build a stock-and-flow model of backlog in a licensing office, and validate it against recorded data.

tasks.title: Map a ministry service into business, data, application and technology layers on an enterprise architecture diagram
Simulate a stock-and-flow model of case backlog with arrivals and processing, and show the effect of hiring staff over 24 months
Validate a set of models through a simulated walkthrough with users, recording defects found and deciding which are severe enough to rework

schedule.title: Change management and capstone defence
schedule.exercise: Present the capstone analysis report, including the business case, models, selected methodology and change plan, and answer a panel on the weakest assumption.

tasks.title: Choose a conversion strategy (parallel, phased, direct) for a payroll replacement and justify it against the risks in the case
Plan training and resistance handling for a clinic system rollout, scoring the plan against the change management rubric
Defend the capstone analysis before a simulated board, responding to challenges on cost, risk, user acceptance and model validity
